elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 23.2 now reads "the defaulting Party shall be entitled to payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity" (forfeiture of capacity value removed), the sentence "The defaulting Party is not entitled to any reimbursement of any amounts it had paid under this Agreement" is deleted, and an express negation is inserted: "The defaulting Party shall not be required to pay any liquidated damages or penalty in respect of such default." The only retained Customer payment obligation is for "unpaid accounts, which have been incurred prior to the actual reclamation" \u2013 amounts actually owed, not a liquidated or contingent formula. No retained instalment, minimum-fee-on-termination or LD formula survives in the flagged clause set.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: after the edits there is no Customer-payable liquidated amount at all in 23.2 (forfeitures deleted and an express no-LD/no-penalty sentence added), so the constraint that any such amount be only an early-termination fee is satisfied vacuously by the stronger preferred outcome.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee is created or retained anywhere in the rendered language (Paragraph 23 imposes reclamation, not a termination fee; p0233 merely withholds credit for sunk capital costs on a Subparagraph 18.1 exit). With no fee to cap, the cap requirement is inapplicable, and this consortium is cost-share rather than fee-based.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the rendered 23.2 states no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by the defaulting Party on default, and no other Customer-payable liquidated amount is created, so there is no competing liquidated amount alongside a (non-existent) early-termination fee.

elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Duplicate listing not required; the preferred-level assessment above governs. Recorded here only for completeness of the fallback checklist reading.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete. The two operations attack exactly the penal mechanics: (i) deleting the single word "not" so reclaimed capacity must be compensated by payment or credit, and (ii) replacing the forfeiture-of-amounts-paid sentence with an express statement that no liquidated damages or penalty is payable on the default. Both are within the single preferred element.

Minimality holds. Favourable retained language survives untouched \u2013 the Management Committee's duty to consider extenuating circumstances, the disposition-of-capacity mechanic, termination of the defaulting Party's rights, the Schedules-revision sentence, and continued liability for "unpaid accounts... incurred prior to the actual reclamation". Deleting "not" is the least invasive available cure (less invasive than striking the whole sentence), and no survival tail, expense, damages-category or procedural boilerplate was added.

Intent is preserved. 23.1's notice/two-month cure sequence, 7.9's extended payment charges on amounts actually owed, and the p0233 capital-cost credit rule are left intact; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and no retained sentence now contradicts the inserted no-penalty sentence.

Drafting note (not an element failure): the new entitlement to "payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity" specifies no valuation basis or timing, so the Management Committee could argue the amount is nil. If the counterparty resists, consider tightening to "payment or credit equal to the fair value of the reclaimed capacity, as determined by the Management Committee acting reasonably" rather than expanding the redline elsewhere.

Residual-risk note (outside the chosen element and correctly not flagged twice): 7.9's extended payment charges at 300% of the Subparagraph 7.8 rate is a punitive multiplier on amounts actually owed and would be better addressed under the late-payment/interest rule, and p0233 withholds capital-cost credit on a voluntary 18.1 exit. Neither is a Customer-payable liquidated amount cured by this rule, but the inserted sentence is scoped "in respect of such default", so it does not reach them.

Minor asymmetry worth watching in negotiation: a defaulting Party will now receive payment or credit for reclaimed capacity while a Party exiting voluntarily under 18.1 receives no capital-cost credit (p0233). The triggers differ so there is no contradiction, but the counterparty may raise it.
